newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN WHITE MARCH MOVEMENT LAUNCHES NEWSPAPER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN WHITE MARCH MOVEMENT LAUNCHES NEWSPAPER.

text.p: Belgium's White March movement, which grew out of the protest by more than 250,000 people in Brussels in October against child murders and police bungling, publishes its first newspaper on Wednesday.

The White March, which costs 20 francs ($0.70), is intended to give people somewhere to air their views about the past failures of the police and justice system to solve the child disappearances that have plagued Belgium, tell their stories and express their hopes for the future.

"There has been lots of talk of high level protection...But there are also lots of cases of local protection, and that is, if anything, worse because they destroy children," Francois-Luc Montulet, Editor in chief of the bilingual newspaper, told a news conference.

The paedophile scandal hit the headlines in August when convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux led police to two captive girls who had been sexually abused, and then to the bodies of four others. He has been charged with murder.

The discoveries led to the October 20 white march in Brussels that shook the political system, not least because it joined the nation's French and Dutch speaking halves in a common cause, and because of the quiet anger they expressed.

The body of another child was discovered in Brussels last month and another convicted child molester, Patrick Derochette has been charged with illegal imprisonment and rape leading to the death of a minor.
Police are still searching for at least six other children who have gone missing in the last seven years.
There are now more than 100 White March committees scattered round Belgium, and almost every weekend there are small marches somewhere in the country.
The next is due to take place at the coastal resort of De Panne, near the French border, on Easter Sunday. Around 5,000 people are expected, according to the organisers.
One idea floated in the first edition of The White March newspaper -- to be published monthly -- is to hold another mass meeting next October 20 to found a national movement for change.
The government has promised changes -- particularly to the parole system for convicted paedophiles, police coordination in investigations and support for the victims and their families.
Dutroux and Derochette were both released early from their respective prison terms.
But the editors of the newspaper and the parents of some of the dead children said the purpose of the periodical was not to be an outlet for outpourings of hate.

"The purpose of this paper is not to be a vehicle for national bile," journalist Michel Lefevre said. "It is not to say everything is ruined. On the contrary it is to say this is a new beginning. The future is in your hands."
